item.title: Now the hard part
item.description: When a country loses a war, the winner dictates the peace terms. This is abundantly clear in the memorandum of understanding. The US and Israel still can’t comprehend that Iran won their war of choice. Also, despite the media hype of ‘Ukraine is winning’ , the reality is that time is running out for Kiev and its western backers. CrossTalking with George Szamuely and Tarik Cyril Amar.

item.title: Poison pills
item.description: We live in grim times. The MoU resolving the US-Israel war on Iran is being sabotaged on multiple fronts. Add to this the Europeans’ refusal to enter into any negotiations or dialogue with Russia to end the war in Ukraine. Overall, peace is not on the agenda. CrossTalking with Patrick Henningsen and Jason Zaharis.

item.title: Iran calls the shots
item.description: Ending the US-Israel war of choice on Iran is proving to be difficult if not impossible. The Americans and Israelis fail to publicly acknowledge they have lost this war. Both have their demands, but Iran has the leverage. Iran is calling the shots. CrossTalking with Sarah Leah Whitson, Mohamed Elmenshawy, and Hicham Safieddine.

item.title: Defeat and humiliation
item.description: At least on paper Iran has won a historic victory over the United States. The MoU demands the US recognize Iran as a legitimate and even powerful state actor. Iran defeated two nuclear states – the US and Israel. Can it now win the peace? CrossTalking with Mohammad Marandi, Ali H. Mourad, and Zaid Belbagi.

item.title: What agreement?
item.description: Not surprisingly the Memorandum of Understanding ending the US-Israel war on Iran means different things to different people. Since its signing, the Trump administration has actively attempted to renegotiate the deal in real time. These attempts haven’t opened the Strait of Hormuz. CrossTalking with Daniel McAdams, Julia Roknifard, and Leila Hudson.

item.title: Defeat and humiliation

Iran defeated two nuclear states – the US and Israel. Can it now win the peace? CrossTalking with Mohammad Marandi, Ali H. Mourad, and Zaid Belbagi.

item.title: End of Sykes-Picot
item.description: As the Americans slow-walk talks and Israel obstructs them, the region and the world is moving on. US Vice President J.D. Vance says Washington hopes to “transform” the Middle East. Well, it has already happened. It’s called the end of the Sykes-Picot era. CrossTalking with Joshua Landis, Ashish Prashar, and Mohammad Khatibi.

item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: Absence of peace
item.description: We are back to square one in Iran and Ukraine. The MOU is looking to be nothing more than a ruse and a deceit. A ploy to buy time and search for leverage. Much the same can be said about the Ukraine conflict. The West is not interested in peace. It is pursuing a policy of direct war against Russia. Russia has taken note. CrossTalking with Mark Sleboda and George Szamuely.

item.title: Agreement-incapable
item.description: As the Iranian people lay to rest their Supreme Leader, Donald Trump has returned to making deadly threats. These threats make a mockery of the Memorandum of Understanding framework aimed at ending the war. This is still more evidence the West is agreement-incapable. CrossTalking with Haytham Faraj, Kevork Almassian, and Mohammed Akunjee.

item.title: Crossing red lines
item.description: NATO’s new wonder weapons for its Ukraine proxy are missiles and drones. The logic is missiles and drones alone will force Russia to end the conflict and surrender. Russia would not dare to escalate to strike NATO in return. This is called brinkmanship and its very dangerous. CrossTalking with Alex Reporterfy, Mats Nilsson, and Alexandre Guerreiro.
